<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 164,000
shares of common stock to an unaffiliated investor, valued at $410,000, or $2.50 per share, as partial consideration for a 100%
working interest in the Wasatch National Forest Well #16-15 and the surrounding 640 acres in Uinta County, Wyoming, known as the
Graham Reservoir Field. The total consideration for this purchase was $610,000, which was paid as follows: (i) $10,000 in cash;
(ii) issuance of 164,000 shares of common stock valued at $410,000, or $2.50 per share; and (iii) issuance of a $190,000 note payable
to the investor.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 485,000
shares of common stock to four unaffiliated investors for cash of $1,212,500 or $2.50 per share. In addition, the Company granted
warrants to purchase up to 242,334 shares of common stock with an exercise price of $2.50 per share, which expire in December 2013.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 100,000
shares of common stock to Thomas R. Grimm, one of the Company&rsquo;s directors, valued at $250,000, or $2.50 per share, as compensation.
The shares issued were fully vested and the value of services received was expensed on the date of grant.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 55,000
shares of common stock to three of our consultants as compensation for their services valued at $137,500, or $2.50 per share. The
shares issued were fully vested and the value of services received was expensed on the date of grant.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 40,000
shares of common stock to a Thomas R. Grimm, one of the Company&rsquo;s directors, for cash of $100,000 or $2.50 per share. In
addition, the Company granted warrants to purchase up to 13,320 shares of common stock with an exercise price of $2.50 per share,
which expire in December 2013.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 170,000
shares of common stock to a noteholder which exercised its right to convert a $425,000 convertible note payable at $2.50 per share.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 15,000
shares of common stock to Joseph P. Tate, one of the Company&rsquo;s directors, valued at $37,500, or $2.50 per share, as payment
for accrued director fees. These shares were fully vested on date of grant.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, an unaffiliated investor
assigned warrants to purchase 34,989 shares of our common stock to an unaffiliated investor for total cash consideration of $6,998,
or $0.20 per warrant. The new warrant holder then exercised the warrants to purchase 34,989 shares of our common stock for total
cash consideration of $55,983, or $1.60 per share.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, one of the Company&rsquo;s
consultants voluntarily returned 10,000 shares of common stock to the Company for cancellation. The shares were issued in December
2009 at a value of $15,000, or $1.50 per share to the consultant as prepayment for services, which were never completed.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 184,072
shares of common stock to five unaffiliated investors, relating to our redemption and conversion of all 285,000 shares of preferred
stock that were outstanding, together with accrued preferred stock dividends totaling $9,515, at a conversion rate of $1.60 per
share.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 62,313
shares of common stock to a noteholder which exercised their right to convert a $100,000 convertible note payable at $1.60 per
share.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">In December 2012, the Company issued 30,750
shares of common stock to one of the Company&rsquo;s creditors as payment of $76,875 or $2.50 per share. This was a negotiated
settlement of a payable.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><I>Treasury Stock</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2012, the Company had
no shares of common stock held as treasury stock. During the year ended December 31, 2012 the Company acquired 254,000 shares of Common Stock valued at $635,000 or $2.50 per share. The Company
retired all 254,000 shares during the year ended December 31, 2012.
During the year ended December 31, 2011, the Company acquired 46,015 valued at cost, for $46,015, or $1.00 per share. The Company
retired 46,015 of the treasury shares valued at $46,015 during the year ended December 31, 2011. The Company accounts for treasury
stock using the cost method.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B></B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>NOTE 13&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;WARRANTS
TO PURCHASE COMMON STOCK</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2012 and December 31,
2011, there were 2,166,874 and 1,269,693 <FONT STYLE="color: black">warrants were outstanding and fully vested, respectively. During
the years ended </FONT>December 31, 2012 and 2011<FONT STYLE="color: black">, warrants totaling </FONT>2,037,497 and 1,269,693
for <FONT STYLE="color: black">shares of common stock were granted. </FONT></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0.8pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Of the total warrants granted during the
year ended December 31, 2012, 935,196 warrants were granted in conjunction with private placements of common stock for cash proceeds
(see NOTE 12 COMMON STOCK) that have an exercise price between $2.50 and $5.00 per share and expire one to three years from the
date of grant and 85,000 warrants were granted in conjunction with a debt settlement that have an exercise price of $2.50 per share
and will expire one year from the date of grant.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Of the total warrants granted during the
year ended December 31, 2011, 69,690 warrants were granted in conjunction with private placements of common stock for cash proceeds
(see NOTE 12 COMMON STOCK) that have an exercise price between $2.50 and $3.00 per share and expire one to two years from the date
of grant.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The fair value of the remaining 1,017,301
and 1,200,003 warrants granted during the years ended December 31, 2012 and 2011, respectively, were <FONT STYLE="color: black">accounted
for by the Company </FONT>under the provisions of FASB ASC 718 and FASB ASC 505. These standards require the Company to record
an expense associated with the fair value of stock-based payments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company uses the Black-Scholes option valuation
model to calculate the fair value of stock-based payments at the date of grant.&nbsp;&nbsp;Warrant pricing models require the input
of highly subjective assumptions, including the expected price volatility.&nbsp;&nbsp;For warrants granted, the Company used a
variety of comparable and peer companies to determine the expected volatility.&nbsp; The Company believes the use of peer company
data fairly represents the expected volatility it would experience if the Company was more actively publicly traded in the oil
and gas industry over the contractual term of the warrants. Changes in these assumptions can materially affect the fair value estimate.&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During the year ended December 31, 2012,
the Company has determined the fair value of the 1,071,301 warrants granted to be $752,503, of which <FONT STYLE="color: black">$448,096
has been expensed as of </FONT>December 31, 2012. The remaining <FONT STYLE="color: black">$304,407 is attributable to forfeited
warrants and will not be expensed in future periods</FONT>.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During the year ended December 31, 2011,
the Company has determined the fair value of the 1,200,003 warrants granted to be $370,772, of which, <FONT STYLE="color: black">$211,208
was expensed as of </FONT>December 31, 2011 <FONT STYLE="color: black">and $83,296 was expensed in 2012. </FONT>The remaining $76,268
was not required to be expensed due to $64,291 <FONT STYLE="color: black">being attributable to a relative fair value adjustment
on notes payable to the Company and</FONT> $11,977 being related to the Freedom Acquisition.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The following is the weighted average of

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>NOTE 14&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;INCOME TAXES</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company utilizes the asset and liability
approach to measuring deferred tax assets and liabilities based on temporary differences existing at each balance sheet date using
currently enacted tax rates in accordance with FASB ASC 740<I>.</I> Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when,
in the opinion of management, it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted for the effects of changes in tax laws and rates on the date of enactment.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The income tax expense for the years ended
December 31, 2012 and 2011 consists of the following:&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">At December 31, 2012 and 2011, the Company
has a net operating loss carry forwards for Federal income tax purposes of $22,546,058 and $18,273,879, respectively, which expire
in varying amounts during the tax years 2017 and 2032. As a result of the Freedom acquisition in 2011 and the corresponding change
in ownership, approximately $7,439,758 of the Company&rsquo;s federal NOL&rsquo;s are subject to a Section 382 limitation resulting
in possible limitations on the future use of these net operating loss carry forwards.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">To date, the Company has generated operating
losses. As a result the Company has recorded a full valuation allowance against its net deferred tax assets as of December 31,
2012 and 2011. The change in the valuation allowance for the years ended December 31, 2012 and 2011 was ($2,396,586) and $5,268,820,
respectively.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Under FASB ASC 740, tax benefits are recognized
only for tax positions that are more likely than not to be sustained upon examination by tax authorities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount
recognized is measured as the largest amount of benefit that is greater than 50 percent likely to be realized upon ultimate settlement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unrecognized
tax benefits are tax benefits claimed in the Company&rsquo;s tax returns that do not meet these recognition and measurement standards.
As of December 31, 2012 and 2011, the Company has no liabilities for unrecognized tax benefits.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s policy is to recognize
potential interest and penalties accrued related to unrecognized tax benefits within income tax expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;For the years
ended December 31, 2012, and 2011, the Company did not recognize any interest or penalties in its consolidated statement of operations,
nor did it have any interest or penalties accrued in its consolidated balance sheet at December 31, 2012 and 2011 relating to unrecognized
tax benefits.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The tax years 2012, 2011, 2010, 2009 and
2008 remain open to examination for federal income tax purposes and by the other major taxing jurisdictions to which the Company
is subject. In addition, due to the fact the Company merged with Freedom, Freedom&rsquo;s tax returns, prior to the merger, for
years 2004 to 2011 also remain open.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0"><B>NOTE 16&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;FAIR VALUE</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-indent: 0.5in"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">FASB ASC 820 defines fair value, establishes
a framework for measuring fair value under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and enhances disclosures about fair value
measurements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Fair value is defined under FASB ASC 820 as the exchange price that would be received for an asset or
paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly
transaction between market participants on the measurement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Valuation techniques used to measure fair value under
FASB ASC 820 must maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The standard describes
a fair value hierarchy based on three levels of inputs, with the first two inputs considered observable and the last input considered
unobservable, that may be used to measure fair value as follows:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Level 1 - Quoted prices in active markets
for identical assets or liabilities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Level 2 - Inputs other than Level 1 that
are observable, either directly or indirectly, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in markets
that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the
full term of the assets or liabilities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Level 3 - Unobservable inputs that are
supported by little or no market activity and that are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As required by ASC 820 financial assets
and liabilities are classified based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement. The Company&rsquo;s
assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement requires judgment and may affect the valuation
of the nonfinancial assets and liabilities and their placement in the fair value hierarchy levels. The fair value of the Company&rsquo;s
asset retirement obligations are determined using discounted cash flow methodologies based on inputs that are not readily available
in public markets.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>

    <DIV STYLE="page-break-before: always; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 6pt"><TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" STYLE="width: 100%"><TR><TD STYLE="text-align: center; width: 100%"><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">RICHFIELD OIL &amp; GAS COMPANY</P><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">Formerly Hewitt Petroleum, Inc.</P><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</P><P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">DECEMBER 31, 2012 AND 2011</P></TD></TR></TABLE></DIV>
    <!-- Field: /Page -->

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company follows the provisions of ASC
820 for nonfinancial assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis. As it relates to the Company, the statement
applies to the initial recognition of asset retirement obligations for which fair value is used.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The asset retirement obligation estimates
are derived from historical costs as well as management&rsquo;s expectation of future cost environments. As there is no corroborating
market activity to support the assumptions used, the Company has designated these liabilities as Level 3. A reconciliation of the
beginning and ending balances of the Company&rsquo;s asset retirement obligation is presented in NOTE 10 ASSET RETIREMENT OBLIGATIONS.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>NOTE 17&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;FINANCIAL
INSTRUMENTS AND CONCENTRATION RISKS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The Company&rsquo;s financial instruments
include cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable and accounts payable. The carrying amount of cash and cash equivalents,
accounts receivable, and accounts payable approximate fair value because of their immediate or short-term maturities.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Substantially all of the Company&rsquo;s
accounts receivable result from oil and natural gas sales or joint interest billings to third parties in the oil and gas industry.&nbsp;&nbsp;This
concentration of customers and joint interest owners may impact the Company&rsquo;s overall credit risk in that these entities
may be similarly affected by changes in economic and other conditions. As of December 31, 2012, 71% of the accounts receivable
balance resulted from two entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2011, 49% of the accounts receivable balances were resulted from
two entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Historically, the Company has not experienced significant credit losses on such receivables.&nbsp;&nbsp;There
was no bad debt was recorded against accounts receivable for the years ended December 31, 2012 and 2011. &nbsp;The Company cannot
ensure that such losses will not be realized in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;For the years ended December 31, 2012 and 2011, all of the
revenues resulted from producing wells in Kansas.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>NOTE 18 LEGAL PROCEEDINGS</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Nostra Terra Oil &amp; Gas Company v.
Richfield Oil &amp; Gas Company</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">On February 1, 2012,
Nostra Terra Oil &amp; Gas Company (&ldquo;NTOG&rdquo;) filed an action against the Company, HPI, HEGINC, and HEGLLC in the Twenty-Third
Judicial District Court of Russell County, Kansas. The complaint alleges that the Company defaulted on its repayment obligations
under a note and security agreement, dated April 13, 2011, in the principal amount of $1,300,000 and accrued interest at 10% per
annum. The complaint seeks foreclosure on two of the Company&rsquo;s property leases located in Kansas. The note was due on January
31, 2012. On January 31, 2012, the Company requested the loan payoff and documents relating to the release of collateral from NTOG&rsquo;s
representatives. The Company followed up on this request with a written request on February 1, 2012. On or about March 19, 2012
the Company filed an answer to the Complaint and a Cross-Complaint against NTOG for tortious interference with business. The previously
set trial date has been cancelled and no trial date currently exists. The Company intends to vigorously defend against this foreclosure
action and repay any amount that is ultimately determined to be outstanding. The obligations due and owing under this note and
security agreement are fully accounted for in the Company&rsquo;s financial statements as of December 31, 2012.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>Litigation in the Ordinary Course</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">We may become involved in litigation from
time to time relating to claims arising in the ordinary course of our business. We do not believe that the ultimate resolution
of such claims would have a material effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition or cash flows. However,
the results of these matters cannot be predicted with certainty, and an unfavorable resolution of one or more of these matters
could have a material effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><B>&nbsp;</B></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">The following
tables present the Company's independent petroleum consultants' estimates of our proved oil and natural gas reserves, as of December
31, 2012 and 2011. As of December 31, 2010, the Company did not have an independent engineering report completed to value its reserves
but relied on internal generated engineering reports and estimates generated by the available data on hand completed by our internal
consultant engineer and staff geologist The Company emphasizes that reserves are approximations and are expected to change as additional
information becomes available. Reservoir engineering is a subjective process of estimating underground accumulations of crude oil
and natural gas that cannot be measured in an exact way, and the accuracy of any reserve estimate is a function of the quality
of available data and of engineering and geological interpretation and judgment.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

factors impacted our total Net Proved Developed and Undeveloped Reserves by the following:</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%" STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt"><TR STYLE="vertical-align: top">
<TD STYLE="width: 13.5pt"></TD><TD STYLE="width: 13.5pt"><FONT STYLE="font-family: Symbol">&middot;</FONT></TD><TD STYLE="text-align: justify">We modified the economic prices from $4.163/MCF for natural gas, and $96.19/Bbl for oil used in
our &ldquo;2011 Pinnacle Reserve Report&rdquo;, attached as Exhibit 99.5 to our Form 10 dated August 17, 2012, to $2.068/MCF for
natural gas and $91.05/Bbl for the Perth and South Haven Fields, $88.45/Bbl for all other Kansas properties, and $84.90/Bbl for
the Wyoming properties used in the 2012 Pinnacle Reserve Report, as of December 31, 2012. The pricing revisions caused our total
Net Proved Developed and Undeveloped Reserves to decrease by 91,987 oil Bbl and to decrease by 57,284 natural gas MCF. Due to our
belief that we will have the necessary financing, we made changes to our two year development plan, including adding 30 net new
drilling locations. These development plan changes caused our Net Proved Undeveloped Reserves to increase by 664,975 oil Bbl and
to increase by 264,653 natural gas MCF. Pricing changes and changes to our two year development plan resulted in an overall increase
in Revisions of Previous Estimates to our total Net Proved Developed and Undeveloped Reserves of 572,988 oil Bbl and 207,369 natural
gas MCF.</TD></TR></TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; background-color: white">Proved reserves
are estimated quantities of oil and natural gas, which geological and engineering data indicate with reasonable certainty to be
recoverable in future years from known reservoirs under existing economic and operating conditions. Proved developed reserves are
proved reserves that can be expected to be recovered through existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods. Proved
undeveloped reserves are included for reserves for which there is a high degree of confidence in their recoverability and they
are scheduled to be drilled within the next five years.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; background-color: white; text-indent: 0.5in"><I>&nbsp;</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; background-color: white"><I>Standardized Measure of Discounted
Future Net Cash Inflows and Changes Therein</I></P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The following table presents a standardized
measure of discounted future net cash flows relating to proved oil and natural gas reserves and the changes in standardized measure
of discounted future net cash flows relating to proved oil and natural gas were prepared in accordance with the provisions of ASC
932-235-50. Future cash inflows were computed by applying oil and natural gas prices that were calculated by using the unweighted
arithmetic average of the first-day-of-the-month price for each month of the 12-month period prior to the ending date of the period,
to estimated future production. Future production and development costs were computed by estimating the expenditures to be incurred
in developing and producing the proved oil and natural gas reserves at the end of the year, based on year-end costs and assuming
continuation of existing economic conditions. Future income tax expenses were calculated by applying appropriate year-end tax rates
to future pretax cash flows relating to proved oil and natural gas reserves, less the tax basis of properties involved and tax
credits and loss carry forwards relating to oil and natural gas producing activities. Future net cash flows are discounted at the
rate of 10% annually to derive the standardized measure of discounted future cash flows. Actual future cash inflows may vary considerably,
and the standardized measure does not necessarily represent the fair value of the Company's oil and natural gas reserves.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0.5in">&nbsp;</P>

    <TD STYLE="font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-bottom: 1pt; padding-left: 0">Net Change in Income Taxes</TD><TD STYLE="font-size: 10pt; padding-bottom: 1pt; padding-left: 0">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-left: 0">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; font-size: 10pt; text-align: right; padding-left: 0">(10,506,966</TD><TD STYLE="padding-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-left: 0">)</TD><TD STYLE="font-size: 10pt; padding-bottom: 1pt; padding-left: 0">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-left: 0">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; font-size: 10pt; text-align: right; padding-left: 0">9,401,409</TD><TD STYLE="padding-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-left: 0">&nbsp;</TD></TR>

    <TD STYLE="font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-bottom: 2.5pt; padding-left: 0">Aggregate Change in the Standardized Measure of Discounted Future Net Cash Flows for the Year</TD><TD STYLE="font-size: 10pt; padding-bottom: 2.5pt; padding-left: 0">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 2.5pt double; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-left: 0">$</TD><TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 2.5pt double; font-size: 10pt; text-align: right; padding-left: 0">11,468,188</TD><TD STYLE="padding-bottom: 2.5pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-left: 0">&nbsp;</TD><TD STYLE="font-size: 10pt; padding-bottom: 2.5pt; padding-left: 0">&nbsp;</TD>
    <TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 2.5pt double; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-left: 0">$</TD><TD STYLE="border-bottom: Black 2.5pt double; font-size: 10pt; text-align: right; padding-left: 0">(10,441,776</TD><TD STYLE="padding-bottom: 2.5pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; padding-left: 0">)</TD></TR>
</TABLE>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: center">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-align: justify">During 2012, there were several factors
that affected our Aggregate Change in the Standardized Measure of the Discounted Future Net Cash Flows for the Year. Net Change
in Sales and Transfer Prices and in Production (Lifting) Costs Related to Future Production from December 31, 2012 and 2011 are
represented by the change in the economic prices used in our engineering reports. We modified the economic prices from $4.163/MCF
for natural gas, and $96.19/Bbl for oil used in our &ldquo;2011 Pinnacle Reserve Report&rdquo;, attached as Exhibit 99.5 to our
Form 10 dated August 17, 2012, to $2.068/MCF for natural gas and $91.05/Bbl for the Perth and South Haven Fields, $88.45/Bbl for
all other Kansas properties, and $84.90/Bbl for the Wyoming properties used in the 2012 Pinnacle Reserve Report, as of December
31, 2012. Net Change Due to Revisions in Quantity Estimates, and Changes in Estimated Future Development Costs, were affected by
a change in our work plan, wherein we added 30 net new wells to our two year development plan, because of our belief that we will
have the necessary financing in order to complete our planned development. Net Change Due to Purchases and Sales of Reserves in
Place was affected by the purchases and sale of several properties. We purchased working interests in several properties, which
had reserves in place, including a 12.00% working interest in the Koelsch Field in Stafford County, Kansas, a 10.00% working interest
in the Perth Field in Sumner County, Kansas and 100% working interest in the Graham Reservoir Field in Uinta County,&nbsp;Wyoming.
The sales of working interest in 2012 included a 5.50% working interest in the Koelsch Field in Stafford County, Kansas. In addition
to these, there where changes in our Standardized Measure of the Discounted Future Net Cash Flow because of associated changes
in Income Taxes, Accretion of Discount, and because of production during the year.</P>

<P STYLE="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0; text-indent: 0.5in"></P>
